SESSION CLOSE 2026-07-31. 23 of 25 child beads closed. Branch phase-0-discipline, pushed, 17 commits from 7210931 to f6f3c4c. 434 tests green on Scala 3.3.8 AND 3.8.4, zero warnings under -Werror, scalafmt clean.

Closed: A1-A6, A5b, B1-B4, C1-C2, D1-D7, G1-G3.
Open: G4 (blocked on real cluster access — see its blocker note) and D6b (filed today after correcting a wrong claim in D6's note).

RESOLUTIONS to the five open decisions recorded in this epic's body:

1. Supersede vs coexist with P7 — SUPERSEDED SEQUENCING ONLY, as proposed. No P7 bead was closed or obsoleted. P7.2, P7.4, P7.6, P6f.12 and P6f.18 remain open and now carry blockers from Phase D. P7.3 was already closed, which unblocked P7.2.

2. Release target — NOT REACHED, deliberately. No baseline was cut; P7.6 remains open and now additionally blocks on D6b. The plan's sequencing holds: the baseline comes after the public surface settles, and D6b is the last known change to that surface.

3. Wire compatibility — RESOLVED EMPIRICALLY, and the answer varied by bead. A2 was additive (flags emitted only when present, so old bytes are unchanged). D1 turned out to need NO wire change at all, because encodeSubmitRequest was already launch-shaped — the approved journal break was not used. D3 and D4 DID change the wire: five SlurmState codes removed, JobRef lost its cluster field, three golden fixtures re-pinned. Nothing is published and no journals exist in the wild, so this cost nothing.

4. Federation — RESOLVED as proposed: unsupported for v0.1, and REFUSED rather than mishandled. A `;cluster` suffix from sbatch --parsable now fails with diagnostic federation-unsupported, while a cluster reported by squeue is retained as evidence. The two surfaces mean opposite things and get opposite treatment; documented in docs/compatibility.md.

5. Phase A branch policy — RESOLVED by default: everything landed on phase-0-discipline with no pre-baseline tag.

ONE ITEM FOR THE OWNER, unchanged from D5: P7.5 (bd-01KYNA5EPTP9Y8QAH1673G613D) is fully absorbed by P8.D5 on the client side and is still open. Its remaining residue is that the AGENT still puts failure.toString on the wire (agent/SchedulerRequestHandler), which is a protocol-module concern for Phase E. Close it or rescope it to that residue; I left it open rather than closing another epic's bead.

RECOMMENDED NEXT: P7.2 (ByteVector) is now genuinely unblocked — its gate P7.3 is closed and the public shape settled through D1-D5 — and it is the prerequisite for P6f.12 and for G3's deferred transport-buffer half. D6b should precede P7.6.
